$comment: What an office's spec must carry: what it answers for, and what it may, must, may-not, and cannot-be-made-to do. A specific office — content/offices/configuration-manager.json — is an INSTANCE of this class, a plain record validated against it; this class is the one schema, and no instance is a schema. An office is the quadruple O = (P, A, D_O, I+): normative structure, the works it governs, deontic profile D_O mapping each governed work to one of {duty, liberty, deontic-power, deontic-immunity}, and the installation morphism. P is the body politic, the normative form whose structure governs the office and exists whether or not any element inhabits it; that is what dignitas non moritur states formally, and it is why this spec carries no incumbent. Incumbency is the double settlement of recognition (the honor axis, backward, history-sensitive) and induction (the munus axis, forward-committed). Vacant is (bottom, bottom); dignitas is (t, t); a top in either is a repair condition. The spec fixes the office; who stands in it is read off those cells.

id.$comment: The record's own name, equal to its basename. An office's address is emsenn/office/<id>, derived from the pool it seats in — never stored as a second fact that can disagree. Resolution is by nearest record from where you stand; a nearer office shadowing a farther one is the rule working.

name.$comment: What the office is called, as it is said: 'configuration manager'. The name a working practitioner of the trade would recognize, never a coinage. An office whose name has to be explained before it can be used was invented rather than derived.

normative-structure.$comment: P — the body politic. What the office answers for, stated as the normative form that persists across incumbents and vacancy. Not a job description: 'a FARS realization that treats office records as job descriptions has lost the substrate's claim that offices are predications.'

additionalProperties.$comment: The four potential Hohfeldian positions, in the enterprise's ruled naming: duty and liberty at act level, deontic-power and deontic-immunity at meta level. Hohfeld wrote 'privilege' for liberty — his worst word, renamed after Glanville Williams — and wrote 'power' and 'immunity' bare, which the enterprise prefixes because both words are already taken, by watts and by biology. The correlatives — claim, no-claim, liability, disability — are derived by the correlative involution and are never authored: the first quartet {claim, duty, liberty, no-claim} and the second {deontic-power, liability, deontic-immunity, disability} are each regular torsors under the Klein four-group generated by correlative and opposite, so naming one corner fixes the other three.

deontic-profile.$comment: The corpus writes D_O : A -> {power, duty, privilege, immunity} — a FUNCTION from what the office governs to Hohfeldian positions, assigned 'independently of any holder'. Two rulings adjust the letter and keep the structure. The domain is work, not bare action: what an office governs is work, per emsenn/schema/deontic-profile, so the keys name works and must resolve to them. The positions carry the ruled names: duty, liberty, deontic-power, deontic-immunity. It is a map and not a list, and that is load-bearing: a work gets exactly one position, so an office cannot both owe a thing and be at liberty about it, which is the SDL consistency invariant made structural. The key set is the work domain — 'no office can be created without articulating what it governs.' First-quartet entries (duty, liberty) are act-level; second-quartet entries (deontic-power, deontic-immunity) are meta-level, over who may alter act-level relations.

bears-duty.$comment: The duty specs this office bears, by address. This list is where the bearer relation LIVES: a duty spec names no bearer, so asking who bears a duty is answered by reading the offices and never by reading the duty. Distinct from the deontic profile's preimage of 'duty', which names works this office is obliged over; this names the separately-specified obligations it has taken up.

provides-skill.$comment: The skills this office's incumbent may invoke, per eligibility-by-skills: an agent's provided set is 'the union of its directly-listed skills plus the skills its offices' duties qualify it to invoke.' Skills are the office's constructors, and they are the one component of an office that is universally F3-formal.

authority-scope.$comment: The office's contribution to the scope fiber — NOT a permission list. An agent's effective scope is the composition of its own scope predicates, its inhabited offices' scope predicates, and any active mode restriction, composed pointwise: concordant restrictions sustain, conflicting restrictions produce top and surface the contradiction for resolution. Offices typically narrow the agent's scope. Scope is computed at substrate-read-time; there is no separate authorization table.

jurisdiction.$comment: The sub-site within which this office's second-quartet powers are operative. Jurisdiction is the four-tuple (A, T_J, H_J, V): outside it, instructions create no valid duties and acts do not propagate. An office with powers and no jurisdiction has powers that are valid nowhere.

distinguished-from.$comment: Offices this one is routinely conflated with. Recorded because the conflation has already happened.

theory-basis.$comment: What the office's structure is derived from. Required, and required to reach a real firm: an office derived from how a session felt from the inside is the failure this key exists to catch. The create-office power's own constraint is that 'the office's structure must be derivable from predicated-governance's office-as-double-settlement and the relevant theory objects.' An office with no theory basis was not derived; it was asserted.

unrealized.$comment: What this office claims and has not built, kept queryable rather than as aspirational prose.

x-agent.$comment: Harness-projection hints for installing-claude-as-an-agent: which model tier, effort, turn budget, and tool allowlist the office's agent runs under. Extension-prefixed because the harness is not doctrine — an office whose work is mechanical can be flowed to a lighter model by its own record, and absent keys inherit the session's defaults.

allOf.$comment: An office naming an upstream concept must say where it resolves.

$comment-absences: No holder/incumbent key: incumbency is the joint affirming settlement of the recognition and induction predicates over a candidate, and an office that could assert its holder would assert a readout. Vacant is not an empty list; it is (bottom, bottom) in that double settlement, alongside munus-only, recognition-only, dignitas, failed, and repair. No duties list separate from bears-duty and the deontic profile: the acts this office is obliged over ARE D_O's preimage of 'duty', and a third list would be a copy that drifts. No accountability key: accountability is the triple (B, S, A) over Outcomes(S), total and non-transferable by delegation — 'delegation distributes authority; it never lifts accountability' — and it does not decompose into the office's per-action positions. No title, no description: name is what it is called, and what it means is the spec body, not a sentence beside it.

workId.$comment: Names a work, per the ruling on emsenn/schema/deontic-profile: what an office governs is work, not bare action.
